title: Reversible and irreversible dynamical topological transitions of magnetic Hopfions
authors: S. Y. Lu, H. M. Dong, D. X. Yu, K. Chang
abstract: Magnetic Hopfions are three-dimensional (3D) topological solitons characterized by a nonzero Hopf invariant and offer a promising platform for 3D spintronics. While their static stabilization has been widely studied, their nonlinear dynamics under alternating magnetic (AM) fields remain largely unexplored. We show, using 3D micromagnetic simulations and analytical mode analysis, that an AM field drives two qualitatively distinct dynamical regimes of a confined magnetic Hopfion. In the weak-field regime, resonant excitation of intrinsic Hopfion modes induces a nonlinear instability and an irreversible topological reconfiguration from a Hopfion to a toron. In contrast, in the strong-field regime, the system undergoes reversible field-locked topological switching at GHz frequencies, with the magnetization periodically alternating between a topologically trivial ferromagnetic configuration and a Hopfion state. The switching pathway is selected by the driving frequency: a 2 GHz field drives a breathing pathway associated with the low-frequency collective response, whereas a 40 GHz field produces a nonresonant rotational pathway governed by strong Zeeman-torque-driven precession and field locking. These results identify field amplitude and frequency as independent control knobs and reveal that reversible Hopfion switching can arise either from nonlinear continuation of low-frequency collective motion or from nonresonant high-frequency field locking.
summary: This paper explores the complex dynamics of magnetic Hopfions under alternating magnetic fields, revealing that the field regime dictates the outcome. Weak fields cause irreversible topological decay, whereas strong fields enable coherent, reversible switching between different topological states. The frequency of the applied field acts as a switch, selecting distinct physical pathways for this controlled topological manipulation.
main_problem: The study investigates how magnetic Hopfions, which are 3D topological solitons, undergo dynamical transitions when subjected to alternating magnetic (AM) fields.
main_result: The system exhibits two distinct regimes: an irreversible transition from Hopfion to toron in weak fields, and a reversible, frequency-dependent switching between ferromagnetic and Hopfion states in strong fields.
method: The research employs 3D micromagnetic simulations combined with analytical mode analysis to track the evolution of topological invariants under time-varying magnetic fields.
model_or_system: The system models magnetization dynamics within a confined nanostructure containing chiral magnetic layers, governed by the Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert equation incorporating exchange, DMI, anisotropy, and dipolar interactions.
key_observables: Hopf invariant (QH), magnetization texture evolution, total energy, and intrinsic mode amplitudes.
important_parameters: Field amplitude ($B_0$) and driving frequency ($f$), which act as independent control knobs determining the switching pathway.
main_assumptions: The dynamics are analyzed by solving micromagnetic equations; the distinction between weak-field (resonant) and strong-field (nonresonant/field-locked) responses is key.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic comparisons of irreversible vs. reversible transitions, time evolution of QH under resonant driving showing breakdown, and detailed temporal traces of magnetization and $Q_H$ for both 2 GHz (breathing) and 40 GHz (rotational) switching pathways.
paper_structure: The paper systematically contrasts the outcomes of weak-field excitation (leading to instability/irreversibility) against strong-field excitation, demonstrating how frequency selects between low-frequency collective motion paths and high-frequency field-locked limit cycles for reversible control.
why_interesting: This work demonstrates controlled topological switching using external fields, providing a platform analogous to controlling quantum states or phase transitions in engineered magnetic systems, which has implications for spintronics and nonlinear dynamics modeling.
